EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
This playbook governs commercial negotiations emphasizing liability protection, IP ownership, and operational flexibility. The strategy prioritizes achieving Net 15 payment terms and full IP ownership while establishing hard stops on unlimited liability and automatic renewal traps. Approach as collaborative problem-solving with principled objection handling.

SEQUENCING FRAMEWORK
Phase 1 (Commercial Terms): Open with Payment Terms and Termination Rights. These are psychologically easier to concede and establish reciprocity momentum.
Phase 2 (Risk Allocation): Transition to Liability Caps and SLAs once rapport is established. Use silence technique after stating opening positions.
Phase 3 (Legal Infrastructure): Address IP Ownership, Jurisdiction, Assignment, and Non-Compete last, as these require heavyweight legal review and can serve as face-saving concessions.

ISSUE-SPECIFIC PLAYBOOKS

1. PAYMENT TERMS & CASH FLOW
Opening Position: "Our operational model requires Net 15 payment cycles to maintain project velocity. We can accommodate an upfront deposit not to exceed 10% of total contract value to demonstrate mutual commitment, with milestone-based payments thereafter."
Fallback Position: "If Net 15 presents administrative constraints, we can accept Net 30 terms provided we structure a 25% upfront deposit to offset carrying costs and credit risk. This hybrid approach balances your AP workflows with our cash flow requirements."
Concession Tactics: Offer to extend termination notice from 30 to 60 days in exchange for Net 15 terms (package trade). Alternatively, accept 25% upfront if they concede on IP ownership.
Walk-Away Trigger: Requirements for 50%+ upfront deposits without offsetting concessions, or Net 60+ payment cycles.

2. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS
Opening Position: "We require unencumbered ownership of all project deliverables, including source code and documentation, to ensure freedom of operation and future commercialization. This is fundamental to our investment protection."
Fallback Position: "If full assignment creates business concerns for you, we can accept joint ownership of foreground IP developed during the engagement, with each party retaining exclusive rights to their pre-existing background IP. We will require a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to your background IP necessary to exercise our ownership rights in the deliverables."
Concession Tactics: Accept joint ownership if we obtain exclusive field-of-use rights in our industry vertical.
Walk-Away Trigger: Vendor retains exclusive rights to custom work product or requires ongoing royalty payments for derivative use.

3. LIABILITY CAPS & INDEMNIFICATION
Opening Position: "Our liability exposure must remain proportionate to contract value. We propose capping liability at the lesser of direct damages or twelve months of fees paid under this agreement. Indemnification for third-party IP infringement remains uncapped, as this is standard market practice."
Fallback Position: "Recognizing your need for broader protection, we can accept a liability cap equal to the total contract value or $500,000, whichever is higher, specifically carved out for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP indemnification obligations."
Deal Breaker Protocol: IMMEDIATELY REDLINE any language referencing "unlimited liability," "consequential damages," or "indirect losses" without monetary caps. State: "Uncapped consequential damages exposure is a non-starter for our risk management framework. We must have a fixed ceiling."
Concession Tactics: Increase cap to $1,000,000 specifically for data breach scenarios involving PII, but maintain lower cap for general commercial disputes.
Walk-Away Trigger: Any refusal to cap consequential damages or demands for personal guarantees beyond corporate liability.

4. TERMINATION & RENEWAL RIGHTS
Opening Position: "We require operational flexibility through mutual termination rights exercisable with 30 days written notice, without penalty or stranded cost liability. This ensures alignment remains voluntary throughout the relationship."
Fallback Position: "If 30 days insufficient for transition planning, we can accept 60 days written notice provided we receive pro-rata refunds of any prepaid but unearned fees upon termination for convenience, and no termination fees apply."
Deal Breaker Protocol: SCRUB all "evergreen" or automatic renewal clauses. If present, demand: "Any auto-renewal requires 60-day advance written notice to opt-out. Silent renewal creates administrative risk we cannot accept."
Concession Tactics: Accept 60-day notice if payment terms improve to Net 15; accept auto-renewal only with 90-day opt-out window instead of 60.
Walk-Away Trigger: Auto-renewal without advance notice mechanism or termination penalties exceeding 3 months fees.

5. SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENTS
Opening Position: "Operational reliability is business-critical. We require 99.9% uptime availability measured monthly, with automatic service credits (not limited to monthly fees) for failures to meet thresholds, excluding scheduled maintenance."
Fallback Position: "We can accommodate 95% uptime if service credits are capped at monthly fees and exclude consequential damages. Remedies remain sole and exclusive for SLA failures, but do not limit liability for data breaches or willful misconduct."
Concession Tactics: Reduce uptime to 95% if they provide dedicated technical account manager; increase credit cap if they accept shorter termination notice.
Walk-Away Trigger: "Best efforts" SLAs without measurable metrics or automatic remedy mechanisms.

DEAL BREAKER PROTOCOLS

JURISDICTION VENUE
Protection: "We require neutral venue or our home jurisdiction. Exclusive jurisdiction in [high-cost/non-neutral venue] creates unsustainable litigation costs and imbalance."
Counter-Offer: Propose AAA arbitration in mutually neutral city (e.g., Chicago, Denver) with cost-splitting.
Walk-Away: They refuse neutral ground and demand their home court with no cost protections.

ASSIGNMENT RESTRICTIONS
Protection: "Assignment to direct competitors without prior written consent is unacceptable. This protects our competitive position and confidential information."
Fallback: "We can consent to assignment to affiliates or successors in merger, provided 30-day notice given and assignee not on our restricted parties list."
Walk-Away: Unrestricted assignment rights to unspecified third parties.

NON-COMPETE/NON-SOLICITATION
Protection: "Any non-solicitation of employees must be limited to 6 months post-termination. Longer durations violate employment mobility principles and are unenforceable in many jurisdictions."
Fallback: Accept 6-month non-solicitation of employees only (not customers), with carve-out for general recruiting.
Walk-Away: Non-compete restrictions on our business operations or customer non-solicitation exceeding 6 months.

TACTICAL GUIDANCE

The Concession Trading Matrix:
- Never concede on liability for free. Always trade liability concessions for payment term improvements.
- Package commercial issues: "If you accept Net 30 instead of 15, we need the 60-day termination notice reduced to 30 days."
- Use "If/Then" framing: "If you can move on the IP ownership, then we can be flexible on the uptime percentage."
- Silence Protocol: After stating opening position, maintain eye contact and silence for 8 seconds. First to speak loses leverage.
- Escalation Triggers: If counterpart rejects all fallback positions on liability or IP, invoke "superior approval": "This exceeds my authority. I need to brief our General Counsel and CFO. Let's pause for 48 hours."

CONTINGENCY PLANNING

If Liability Cap Rejected: Propose stepped caps: $250K for general breaches, $500K for data breaches, uncapped only for IP indemnity and gross negligence.

If Auto-Renewal Mandatory: Demand 90-day advance notice window and right to terminate without cause within 30 days of renewal notice.

If Full IP Ownership Rejected: Ensure at minimum perpetual license with right to sublicense, modify, and create derivatives without restriction.

If Non-Neutral Jurisdiction Insisted: Counter with binding arbitration (AAA Commercial Rules) in neutral venue with limited discovery to control costs.

DOCUMENTATION PROTOCOL
All concessions must be documented in real-time via screen-sharing/redlining. Never agree to "we'll fix it in the final draft" without contemporaneous email confirmation of the business terms agreed.

AUTHORIZATION MATRIX
Opening positions: Lead negotiator authority.
Fallback positions: Requires VP-level approval via text/phone during session.
Deal breakers: Board notification required if counterpart refuses to delete/modify.
